sections.hypothesis: btc-rotation-8 (G1), traded forward through Kestrel on Binance's Spot Testnet, (a) behaves exactly as the backtest model says it should, and (b) beats BTC held over data that didn't exist when it was designed.
sections.rationale: On pursue since 2026-11-16 (Luke). Found in exploration round 2 and confirmed on the unspent holdout year of 8 coins it had never seen (flat while BTC fell 29%, against -4.7% for BTC at its 18% exposure); on its own coins 2018-25 it fails only luck and walk-forward (5 of 11). Its coins' holdout years are now spent, so forward data is the remaining test. Minimum track record from its backtest daily returns (Bailey and Lopez de Prado): 218 days for 90% confidence that its true Sharpe is above zero (359 for 95%); it runs 395 days, matching the other paper accounts, so all are reviewed together. It leans on BTC's trend, as trend-vol-target and btc-regime-trend do; running all three shows whether it adds anything. All 8 coins trade on the Spot Testnet (checked 2026-11-16). The testnet proves the plumbing; its prices come from the test order book, so the strategy is judged on the model replay at real Binance prices, which makes the same decisions by construction.
sections.rules: One account, rot-g1: kestrel paper open rot-g1 --symbol UNIVERSE --strategy btc-rotation-8 --research <this note> --venue testnet --cash 330, then kestrel paper schedule rot-g1 (hourly at 10 past; idempotent). Before it opens, the paper runner must trade a basket strategy (it trades one coin per account today): every coin in the set refreshed with the quality check, decisions at each Sunday close, orders per coin at the next open through the shared rebalance step, a ledger per coin position, reconciliation for every held coin, and a day-by-day replay that reproduces the portfolio backtest exactly (the same test the single-coin accounts pass). Default settings (top 3 of BTC, ETH, SOL, BNB, DOGE, LINK, DOT, LTC by 90-day return, each Sunday while BTC closes 3% above its 50-day average, each slot sized to 50% volatility), daily bars, the [risk] limits in kestrel.toml. Runs 395 days from its first decision. Reviewed every 3 months with kestrel paper track and the Trading page. Interim reviews report; only the 6-month check can end it, and only for failure.
sections.falsification: Plumbing, at every review: any decision that differs from the model is a bug, fixed before the test continues (not a strategy failure); missed days must stay under 5% of days handled; an order refused for Binance's minimum is reported. Early failure, at 182 days only: if the model replay is behind BTC held at its average exposure on both Sharpe and return, Claude recommends stopping and Luke decides. Strategy, at 395 days: the model replay must (1) have a probabilistic Sharpe of at least 90%, (2) beat BTC held at its average exposure over the whole period, by Sharpe if BTC's Sharpe is positive and by return if it isn't, and (3) keep its worst drawdown no deeper than 50%. Failing any one means Claude recommends drop and Luke decides. Reported beside the other paper accounts over the same days, deciding nothing. A safety halt pauses the test for Luke to decide; it isn't resumed without a recorded reason.
sections.parameters: top_n 3, lookback_days 90, btc_days 50, margin_pct 3, vol_days 30, target_vol_pct 50 (the defaults; never changed during the test).
sections.costs: Modelled at kestrel.toml's costs (7.5 bps fees with the BNB discount, plus each coin's spread band). Until the venue handles BNB fees, testnet fills pay 10 bps, so tracking will show fees slightly above the model. At 330 USDT a volatility-sized slot is roughly 20-110 USDT, above Binance's 5 USDT minimum. Paper trading is not a trial: nothing is chosen from it.
